review_note: Pinned lines 4368–4385 define c by the minimum dimension of a closed subset disconnecting the complement in X and d by the minimum dimension of an irreducible component of X. For complete Noetherian local A and proper I the strict numerical bound on dim Z implies Y\Z connected; the punctured Spec(A/I) criterion is separately retained. Source reference text adds no hypothesis.
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian complete local ring.
Let $I$ be a proper ideal of $A$.
Set $X = \Spec(A)$ and $Y = V(I)$.
Denote
\begin{enumerate}
\item $d$ the minimal dimension of an irreducible component of $X$, and
\item $c$ the minimal dimension of a closed subset $Z \subset X$
such that $X \setminus Z$ is disconnected.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
for $Z \subset Y$ closed we have $Y \setminus Z$ is connected if
$\dim(Z) < \min(c, d - 1) - \text{cd}(A, I)$. In particular, the punctured
spectrum of $A/I$ is connected if $\text{cd}(A, I) < \min(c, d - 1)$.

review_note: Source lemma lines 4447–4461 has I-adically complete Noetherian A with dualizing complex, strict prime-specialization dimension bound for minimal p outside V(I), and connectedness of every nonempty open neighbourhood of V(I)\V(a). Its conclusion is that locus is EMPTY OR CONNECTED, not necessarily nonempty. The draft exactly retains this disjunction.
statement:
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item if $\mathfrak p \subset A$ is a minimal prime not contained
in $V(I)$ and $\mathfrak q \in V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(\mathfrak a)$, then
$\dim((A/\mathfrak p)_\mathfrak q) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$,
\item any nonempty open $V \subset \Spec(A)$ which contains
$V(I) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$ is connected\footnote{For example
if $A$ is a domain.}.
\end{enumerate}
Then $V(I) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$ is either empty or connected.

\label{lemma-connected}
Let $I \subset \mathfrak a$ be ideals of a Noetherian ring $A$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is $I$-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
\item if $\mathfrak p \subset A$ is a minimal prime not contained
in $V(I)$ and $\mathfrak q \in V(\mathfrak p) \cap V(\mathfrak a)$, then
$\dim((A/\mathfrak p)_\mathfrak q) > \text{cd}(A, I) + 1$,
\item any nonempty open $V \subset \Spec(A)$ which contains
$V(I) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$ is connected\footnote{For example
if $A$ is a domain.}.
\end{enumerate}
Then $V(I) \setminus V(\mathfrak a)$ is either empty or connected.

review_note: Pinned source lines 4478–4487 requires A a Noetherian domain with dualizing complex, f a nonzero completion parameter, f∈a, and every irreducible component of V(a) of codimension >2 in Spec A (equivalently >1 in V(f)). It concludes V(f)\V(a) connected; no weakened codimension or extra nonemptiness claim has been added.
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian domain which has a dualizing complex
and which is complete with respect to a nonzero $f \in A$.
Let $f \in \mathfrak a \subset A$ be an ideal.
Assume every irreducible component of $Z = V(\mathfrak a)$
has codimension $> 2$ in $X = \Spec(A)$, i.e., assume every
irreducible component of $Z$ has codimension $> 1$ in $Y = V(f)$.
Then $Y \setminus Z$ is connected.
